organizations.nameVariants: Orkiestra Teatru Perskie Oko; Perskie Oko Theatre Orchestra
organizations.publicNote: Local heading for the theatre orchestra named on the linked Syrena Grand Record discs. The sources identify Zygmunt Wiehler as conductor but do not establish the orchestra’s full personnel; the ensemble is distinct from Teatr “Perskie Oko” itself.

sources.shortCitation: Syrena Grand Record 17919, “Jak się da, to się zrobi!” (1926)
sources.fullCitation: Katalog Polskich Płyt Gramofonowych, record no. 38213. Syrena Record, 1926: “Jak się da, to się zrobi!” (side number 17919), coupled with “A zresztą, niech pan zadzwoni!” (side number 17921); both credited to Bruno Asper. Conductor: Zygmunt Wiehler.
sources.title: Jak się da, to się zrobi! — Syrena Grand Record 17919, catalogue entry
sources.creator: Perskie Oko Theatre Orchestra; Zygmunt Wiehler, conductor
sources.researchNote: The catalogue dates the disc to 1926 and lists 17919 and 17921 as its two side numbers; it does not separately identify them as matrix numbers. The displayed label in the Stare Melodie transfer independently names the Perskie Oko theatre orchestra and conductor Z. Wiehler. The KPPG entry does not identify a lyricist or sheet-music publisher; those credits are supported by separate printed sources.

sources.shortCitation: Syrena Grand Record 17921, “A zresztą… niech pan zadzwoni” (1926)
sources.fullCitation: Orkiestra teatru „Perskie Oko”, conducted by Z. Wiehler. “A zresztą… niech pan zadzwoni.” Shimmy. Syrena Grand Record, no. 17921. Transfer from a privately held disc published by Stare Melodie on YouTube, 10 April 2025.
sources.title: A zresztą… niech pan zadzwoni — Syrena Grand Record 17921
sources.creator: Orkiestra teatru „Perskie Oko”; Zygmunt Wiehler, conductor
sources.researchNote: The displayed label confirms the title, orchestra, conductor Z. Wiehler and number 17921. The uploader reports 1926 and calls 17921 the matrix as well as the disc number; the label image alone does not establish a separate matrix number. KPPG record 38213 independently dates the coupled 17919/17921 disc to 1926. The upload description credits Henryk Chwast under the pseudonym Bruno Asper; both forms are independently documented as Kaper’s pseudonyms.
